svg.text: Layouts are holders of objects, like slides, but in their own list. A placeholder is an ordinary object with a purpose (the label people see); an object that copies one is marked bound_to_placeholder (technical).
A template is not a class of its own: it is a presentation without slides, read through a view.
layouts: dict[id, Layout] # ids l1, l2…
first(): the one a new deck starts on
to_name: bool # provisional, named after parent
· not a Thing: no # reference, own namespace
holder: str # slide or layout id
· slide object: the placeholder it copies
· no new kind: a placeholder is
a text object with a style
# the deck's own copy, whatever its origin
template_origin: str | None # a note only
empty(): basic layout, slide s1 on it
· a bound object’s frame is a copy of the layout’s
· a read view over a presentation
· without slides; not stored as a class
its own copy of a theme’s parts
· rebind worked out by the model, carried
as final values (Q22): the same purpose
follows, else a free box at its frame
· object: bound to a placeholder, or an
object of the layout itself (a logo)
· makes the provisional layout, applies the
change, puts the slide on it; one undo step
move the placeholder, put the slides back
the provisional layout; settle copies frames
Bound objects are copies, refreshed after every command (settle); commands may not change a bound frame. Purpose labels are unique within a layout; a slide’s layout exists.
So moving a bound object on a slide is not a command of its own: the offer flow turns it into DeviateLayout. Details: sheet 5.
